summary: This is a JUnit test that creates a Thermostat set to a low temperature and checks that its status reads "Heating". It is the smallest useful unit test: one object, one expected value, one assertion.

lines.text: Brings in the @Test annotation from JUnit 5, which is how you mark a method as a test the framework should run.
A static import lets you write assertEquals(...) directly instead of Assertions.assertEquals(...), which keeps the test body short and readable.
Tests live in their own class, named after the class under test plus the suffix Test. This convention is what tools use to find your tests.
Marks the method below as a test case. Without this annotation JUnit ignores the method entirely.
The method name is a sentence describing the expected behaviour, so a failure report tells you what broke without you having to read the code. Test methods need no parameters and return nothing.
Sets up the situation being tested by constructing a thermostat at 60 degrees, a value deliberately below the target so the heating branch is the one exercised.
Compares the expected value against what the method actually returned; the expected value always comes first. If the two differ, JUnit fails the test and prints both.
